title: The Coming Wave
author: Mustafa Suleyman with Michael Bhaskar
blurb: Mustafa Suleyman, a co-founder of DeepMind, argues that humanity is about to be hit by a new wave of technology, led by artificial intelligence and synthetic biology. History shows that general-purpose technologies spread relentlessly once they work, getting cheaper and more accessible until almost anyone can use them. This wave is different because its tools are cheap, fast-evolving, useful for nearly everything, and increasingly autonomous. That creates what he calls the containment problem: how do we keep control of technologies that could empower tiny groups to cause enormous harm? He warns of a grim dilemma. Failing to contain the wave risks catastrophe, while clamping down too hard risks a surveillance-heavy dystopia. His answer is a narrow path of layered steps, from safety engineering and audits to laws, alliances and culture, that together could make containment possible.

lessons.b: Once a general-purpose technology works, it spreads, gets cheaper and becomes nearly impossible to stop, as history repeatedly shows.

lessons.t: AI and Synthetic Biology Lead the Wave
lessons.b: Artificial intelligence and the ability to engineer life are the twin technologies driving the next wave, and they amplify each other.

lessons.t: Four Traits That Make This Wave Different
lessons.b: This wave is uniquely hard to control because it is asymmetric, hyper-evolving, omni-use and increasingly autonomous.

lessons.t: Why Nobody Wants to Slow Down
lessons.b: Powerful incentives like profit, national rivalry and curiosity push the wave forward, while pessimism aversion stops us from facing the risks.
